notes.2: A number of candidates chose D . This was probably based on it being the lightest of the balls.
notes.3: A number of weaker candidates calculated the uphill speed and the downhill speed and took the average of the two calculations. Rather, the average speed is the total distance travelled (600 m) divided by the total time taken (75 s).
notes.8: Although stronger candidates answered this correctly, all of the other options were chosen by a significant number of candidates.
notes.9: Many candidates found this question challenging and only the strongest answered correctly.
notes.11: A large number of candidates forgot to include the gravitational field strength in their calculation.
notes.12: Many candidates had difficulty with this question, and all opinions were popular. Stronger candidates knew the formula for pressure and were careful about unit conversions.
notes.13: A number of candidates were unaware of the equation p = ρ gh , even though it is explicitly required by the syllabus.
notes.17: A significant number of candidates chose option B, but stronger candidates answered correctly.
notes.20: A significant number of candidates selected option B despite the lack of meaning of ‘conductor of radiation’.
notes.21: Although stronger candidates answered correctly, many other candidates chose option A.
notes.22: A number of candidates forgot to take the sines of the angles.
notes.24: A number of weaker candidates chose option C . They only needed to continue the two rays on the question paper to discover their error.
notes.27: Candidates were not expected to know any of the relative velocities, but they should know that sound travels considerably faster in solids than in gases or liquids.
notes.30: A large number of candidates believed that positive ions can move around in a metal. It is only the electrons that do the moving.
notes.31: With the switch closed, the voltmeter is simultaneously measuring the p.d. across the resistor and the e.m.f. of the cell.
notes.35: Stronger candidates were able to apply N p / N s = V p / V s , but not, apparently, I p V p = I s V s.
notes.general_comments: Many of the questions were answered correctly by the majority of candidates.
